item.content:encoded:
In Gujarat, three people were killed on the spot after a speeding car overturned and caught fire in Gujarat’s Junagadh district early this morning. The incident occurred around 5 AM near Khamidana village on the Keshod-Balagam road.

According to Keshod Police, four people were travelling in the vehicle when the driver lost control while negotiating a turn at high speed. The car overturned, hit a roadside stone, and immediately burst into flames.

While three occupants were trapped inside and died in the blaze, a young woman miraculously survived after being thrown clear of the burning vehicle. She was rushed to the Keshod Government Hospital via a 108 ambulance for medical treatment. Police and fire brigade teams reached the spot and have launched a further investigation into the mishap.

item.content:encoded:
In Rajasthan, nine members of a family, were killed and seven others injured in a tragic road accident on the Kota-Udaipur National Highway near Shambhupura this morning. According to police, the accident occurred when a speeding Cruiser vehicle carrying family members rammed into a truck parked along the roadside.
 
The victims were residents of Maharashtra’s Dhule district and were returning home after visiting Khatu Shyamji temple in Sikar district of the state. The vehicle was reportedly carrying 16 family members at the time of the accident. Kota City Superintendent of Police Tejaswani Gautam and other administrative officials reached the accident site and supervised rescue operations. The injured were rushed to the New Medical College Hospital in Kota, where they are undergoing treatment. 
 
Governor Haribhau Bagde expressed sorrow over the tragic incident and extended his condolences to the families of the deceased. He wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

item.content:encoded:
Jammu and Kashmir is likely to witness largely dry weather conditions until the end of November. MeT Department forecast a fall of 1-2 degrees Celsius in minimum temperatures across the region during the coming days. According to the MeT department the weather is expected to remain generally dry between today to November 30, while partly to generally cloudy conditions are likely from December 1 to 3.

The minimum temperatures are likely to decline by 1-2 degrees Celsius towards the end of November, indicating colder nights across the Kashmir Valley and other parts of Jammu and Kashmir. The MeT department has advised people to keep track of subsequent weather updates as temperatures are expected to fall towards the closing days of November.

item.content:encoded:
In Gujarat, seven people, including three children, were killed in a tragic road accident near Khavda in Kutch district late last night. According to official reports, the collision occurred on the Bhuj-Khavda National Highway when a car rammed into a trailer.

The impact of the crash was so severe that the car was completely mangled. All seven victims are suspected to be members of the same family. Upon receiving information, local police and emergency rescue teams rushed to the spot. The bodies have been sent to the hospital for post-mortem examination. Police have registered a case to investigate the exact cause of the accident.

item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: Acclaimed French filmmaker and screenwriter Julie Bertuccelli said that Documentary cinema has the power to take audiences closer to the lives, struggles and experiences of voiceless people. Artistic freedom, social responsibility and ethical engagement with real-life subjects were discussed in a masterclass today at IFFI. Julie Bertuccelli was in conversation with National Award-winning Indian […]
item.content:encoded:
Acclaimed French filmmaker and screenwriter Julie Bertuccelli said that Documentary cinema has the power to take audiences closer to the lives, struggles and experiences of voiceless people.  
 
Artistic freedom, social responsibility and ethical engagement with real-life subjects were discussed in a masterclass today at IFFI. Julie Bertuccelli was in conversation with National Award-winning Indian filmmaker Haobam Paban Kumar.
 
Mr. Bertuccelli said that making a documentary could significantly and dangerously affect the lives of its subjects.
 
Mr Bertuccelli said she preferred films that offered hope and encouragement rather than merely highlighting the negative aspects of society.
 
filmmaker said that ideas could emerge from unexpected encounters, a place or an issue. She said that while a script was often necessary to approach producers, the actual process remained open to the unpredictability of real life.
Ms Bertuccelli said that implications of AI extended beyond concerns about creativity and copyright infringement. They include its environmental costs.
 
She cautioned against excessive dependence on AI, which can undermine human memory and independent thinking. She believes that AI can never create spontaneous emotions, silences, gestures and imperfections of real human interactions.

item.content:encoded: The Jammu and Kashmir Government has accorded administrative approval for the construction and establishment of a tourism resort at Kesri Hills in the Budhal area of Rajouri district at an estimated cost of Rs. 7.97 crore. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the proposed tourism resort is aimed at strengthening tourism infrastructure in the Pir Panjal region and unlocking the tourism potential of the area, known for its scenic landscapes and rich natural and cultural heritage. The initiative is expected to give a boost to tourism-related activities, create livelihood and employment opportunities for local residents, and provide visitors with improved facilities to explore the natural beauty of the region. The project marks another step by the J&K Government towards promoting lesser-explored tourist destinations and expanding the tourism footprint of Jammu and Kashmir beyond established tourist circuits.

item.content:encoded:
The Indian Panorama section was inaugurated today at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa, with Aditya Dhar’s blockbuster film ‘Dhurandhar’ selected as the opening film in the Feature Film category under the Mainstream Cinema section.
 
Addressing the media, actor Rakesh Bedi, who portrayed Jameel Jamali in the film, shared his experiences of working on ‘Dhurandhar’. He said his continued association with theatre helped him prepare for the role, which was different from his earlier performances, most of which were comic in nature.
 
The film’s art director, Saini Johray, spoke about the challenges of recreating Lyari on the sets. He said he studied archival footage, newspaper clippings and three-dimensional maps of the actual location to ensure an authentic representation of the area in the film.

item.title: Manipur spurious liquor incident: Death toll rises to 16
item.dc:creator: News On AIR
item.description: The death toll in the suspected spurious liquor incident in Chandel district of Manipur has risen to 16. Around 600 people have been admitted to various government and private hospitals, while 12 patients are currently undergoing treatment in Intensive Care Units. Addressing a press conference at Imphal, Commissioner of Excise, Government of Manipur, Hungyo […]
item.content:encoded:
The death toll in the suspected spurious liquor incident in Chandel district of Manipur has risen to 16. Around 600 people have been admitted to various government and private hospitals, while 12 patients are currently undergoing treatment in Intensive Care Units.
 
Addressing a press conference at Imphal, Commissioner of Excise, Government of Manipur, Hungyo Worshang, said that teams from the district administration, police, excise and health departments have visited the affected areas and hospitals to assess the situation and provide necessary assistance. He informed that six persons have been arrested in connection with the incident. 
 
Samples of the suspected liquor have been sent for forensic examination to identify the presence of toxic substances. The State Government has also constituted a high-level inquiry committee to investigate the incident, identify possible lapses and recommend necessary action. The committee has been asked to submit its report within one month.
 
Meanwhile, Director of Health Services, Dr N Hemantakumar, said that the Health Department has issued a public health advisory in view of the suspected spurious liquor-related deaths and illnesses. He urged anyone who had consumed liquor from suspected sources during the last 48 to 72 hours to seek immediate medical evaluation, even if they have no symptoms.
 
The Health Department has directed all government and private healthcare facilities to remain alert and ensure prompt treatment, referral and reporting of suspected cases. People have also been urged to preserve suspected liquor bottles and containers, if available, and report any illegal sale or distribution of liquor to the police or excise authorities.
 
The State Government has appealed to the public to remain vigilant and cooperate with the authorities to prevent further loss of lives.

item.title: Historical ties have brought SCO countries closer: Union Minister Gajendra Shekhawat
item.dc:creator: News On AIR

Addressing the joint sessions on the second day of the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi today, he said civilisations are not merely […]
item.content:encoded:
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) countries closer to one another. Addressing the joint sessions on the second day of the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi today, he said civilisations are not merely legacies of the past but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate the present and inspire future generations. 
 
Mr Shekhawat emphasised that the shared civilizational knowledge and heritage should be harnessed to advance collective efforts through dialogue, institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges, and meaningful cooperation. He expressed confidence that the Forum would emerge as a lasting platform for fostering civilizational understanding and strengthening cultural ties among the SCO nations.
 
Meanwhile, Culture Secretary Vivek Agarwal has said that the SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum provides an important opportunity for the member states to understand their rich cultural heritage, historical connections, and shared civilizational values, while facilitating the exchange of ideas.
 
The second day of the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue Forum witnessed deliberations on cultural expressions of civilisations, art and architecture, and historical trade relations.
